bmt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Law of cosines in one rhombus corner
bmt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let $A$ be the vertex of the octagon next to $W$ and $X$. Each rhombus has side $1$, so $AW=AX=1$. The interior angle of the octagon at $A$ is $135^\circ$, and the two other rhombus corners at $A$ each take $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$, so $\angle WAX=135^\circ-2\cdot45^\circ=45^\circ$.

Then $WX^2=1^2+1^2-2\cos45^\circ=2-\sqrt2$. By symmetry $WXYZ$ is a square, so its area is $WX^2=2-\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2-\sqrt2$**

bmt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Angles at $A$
bmt-2023-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
Since $3^2+4^2=5^2$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. $A$ lies on the straight line $PQ$, so $\angle PAB+\angle BAC+\angle CAQ=180^\circ$, and with $\angle PAB=\angle QAC$ each equals $45^\circ$ ($B$ and $C$ are on the same side of $PQ$).

Put $A=(0,0)$ with $PQ$ along the $x$-axis, $P$ to the left: $B=3(\cos135^\circ,\sin135^\circ)=\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt2},\frac3{\sqrt2}\right)$ and $C=4(\cos45^\circ,\sin45^\circ)=\left(\frac4{\sqrt2},\frac4{\sqrt2}\right)$.

The center $O=(x,0)$ satisfies $OB=OC$: $\left(x+\frac3{\sqrt2}\right)^2+\frac92=\left(x-\frac4{\sqrt2}\right)^2+8$, i.e. $\frac{14}{\sqrt2}x=7$, $x=\frac{\sqrt2}2$. Then $r^2=OB^2=\left(\frac{\sqrt2}2+\frac3{\sqrt2}\right)^2+\frac92=8+\frac92=\frac{25}2$.

The semicircle has area $\frac12\pi r^2=\frac{25\pi}{4}$.

**Answer: $\frac{25\pi}{4}$**
